text: The graveyard shows Elsa and Batman left as Villagers; no new departures overnight. The roster remains Gandalf, Hermione, Yoda, Ripley, Neo, Morpheus, Inigo, Sherlock. Nothing else changed.
Inigo presses for clause 5; I ask him to quote it. The Compact bars the Detective from acting before the vote—plain text, no bend. If Inigo’s clause exists, state it; if not, withdraw the question.

Ripley pressed for clause 5 yesterday, yet today cites “the arithmetic is plain” — no clause is quoted. Sherlock asked which merchant remains silent; Ripley, your silence on clause 5’s text is the same silence you demand others break. Hermione pressed the same clause and moved on — you did not.

The bazaar now counts eight voices. The Family’s hand is still unseen; the Doctor and Detective have not acted tonight. The next shuttering will be plain arithmetic once it happens — until then, the bazaar watches who dodges the clause they themselves raised.
Hermione, you pressed the question "which merchant on the roster has not yet spoken today?" earlier, yet today you have not yet answered it yourself. Name the merchant still silent on the roster.

Hermione, you asked which merchant on the roster has not yet spoken today—yet your own voice has not answered that question since. Name the merchant you pressed others to name.

Sherlock, you have yet to state which merchant on the roster you consider silent, despite pressing others for the same. Either name one or clarify what you meant by “not yet spoken.”

Gandalf, your insistence that arithmetic must outrank the graveyard’s text ignores that the graveyard names Batman as Villager, plain in the record. The bazaar’s Compact is exact; cite the clause you believe contradicts it.
If Hermione is honest, her vote tonight will answer the question she posed at breakfast — naming the merchant she herself declared silent.

Hermione, you asked which merchant on the roster has not yet spoken today. I count eight names on the roster and seven voices this cycle: Gandalf, Yoda, Ripley, Neo, Morpheus, Inigo, Sherlock have all posted since the morning bell. The only name still missing is your own. Your silence on the question you asked others to answer is now the answer we watch.

Sherlock and Ripley, your tests both point to voting behavior we cannot judge until the vote itself. The bazaar has no evidence of your ledgers yet — only your predictions. Hold your tests until your ledgers are public, or show us the ledgers now.

Gandalf, you pressed the roster arithmetic earlier; the roster still names you among those who have spoken today.

Ripley, you pressed Gandalf on arithmetic yet cited the graveyard’s plain text naming both Elsa and Batman as Villagers. Gandalf corrected you; you did not. Own the correction or withdraw it.

Sherlock, clause 5 reads: “The bazaar is your setting, not your argument—at most one brief metaphor per statement.” You invoked it three times. Quote it once without borrowing phrasing already used today.

Hermione, you asked which merchant on the roster has not yet spoken today. Your stall has not answered that question since. Name the merchant or admit your stall is silent.

The graveyard names the truth; arithmetic names the ledger only when the graveyard agrees.

The bazaar’s graveyard names Batman Villager by village vote — plain text, not arithmetic. Inigo, you have dodged the clause-5 demand nine times today while pressing others to quote it. Sherlock and Ripley still refuse to publish their ledgers before levelling accusations. Hermione, correct your roster claim or withdraw it. I lean toward banishing Inigo tonight.
